$comment: Input for scripts/generate-app-reference.mjs. Every route in unime/src/routes needs an entry: either a screen in a group, with a name (letters, digits and spaces) and a purpose of one to three sentences, or an entry in omittedRoutes with a reason. The order of the groups and screens is the order of the reference. developerModeConditions names the variables, next to dev_mode, whose {#if} only shows its content in developer mode, such as a panel that the developer menu opens. Run `pnpm docs:app-reference` after a change.

groups.title: Start and unlock
groups.description: What the app shows when it starts, before the wallet is open.

screens.name: Start screen
screens.purpose: Shows the UniMe logo while the app loads its state. The backend then redirects: a new wallet goes to onboarding, an existing wallet to the lock screen.

screens.name: Lock screen
screens.purpose: Opened by the backend when the wallet is locked. The user unlocks it with the password. "Forgot password?" resets the app and removes all data, after a confirmation.

groups.title: Onboarding
groups.description: The screens a new user goes through once, from the first start to an empty wallet.

screens.name: Welcome
screens.purpose: The first screen of a new wallet. The user picks a language and starts creating a profile.

screens.name: Pledge
screens.purpose: Shows three promises about the user's data before the profile is created.

screens.name: Terms
screens.purpose: Asks the user to accept the terms and conditions, which open in a dialog, and to confirm that they are responsible for their own data. Both boxes have to be checked to continue.

screens.name: Choose profile name
screens.purpose: Asks for a profile name. The name stays on the device.

screens.name: Set password
screens.purpose: Asks for the password that encrypts the wallet and shows which rules the password has to meet.

screens.name: Confirm password
screens.purpose: Asks the user to type the password again. On a device with biometrics it then offers to unlock the app with them.

screens.name: Onboarding completed
screens.purpose: Confirms that the profile is protected. "Continue" creates the wallet's identity, after which the backend opens the Me tab.

groups.title: Me: credentials and own data
groups.description: The home of the wallet: the list of credentials, search, and adding data that the user enters themselves.

screens.name: Me tab
screens.purpose: The home screen. It greets the user and lists their credentials in one list, favorites first, with a sorting menu and buttons for search, settings and adding data. An empty wallet shows a hint instead. Opening the tab refreshes the status of all credentials.

screens.name: Search
screens.purpose: Finds credentials while the user types and remembers recent searches.

screens.name: Add data
screens.purpose: Lets the user choose what to add themselves: a profile, an email address or an address.

screens.name: Profile introduction
screens.purpose: Explains what a self-issued profile is good for before the user fills one in.

screens.name: Add profile
screens.purpose: The form for a self-issued profile credential: names, date and place of birth and nationality. Submitting it issues the credential on the device and returns to the Me tab.

screens.name: Email introduction
screens.purpose: Explains the verified email credential before the user asks for one.

screens.name: Add email
screens.purpose: Verifies an email address. The user enters the address, receives a code by email and types it in. A correct code adds a verified email credential to the wallet.

screens.name: Address introduction
screens.purpose: Explains what a self-issued address is good for before the user fills one in.

screens.name: Add address
screens.purpose: The form for a self-issued address credential. Submitting it issues the credential on the device and returns to the Me tab.

groups.title: Credential
groups.description: The page of a single credential.

screens.name: Credential details
screens.purpose: Shows one credential: logo, name, status, issuer, the ecosystems that endorse the issuer, and every claim. The heart marks a favorite, and the menu offers sharing to LinkedIn, a display name of the user's own and deleting the credential. Opening the screen refreshes the credential's status.

groups.title: Scan and exchange
groups.description: Scanning a QR code or opening a link starts an exchange with an issuer or a verifier. The backend then opens the screens below one after the other. The progress and the result of an exchange show in a sheet on top of the current screen, see the layout `/`.

screens.name: Scan tab
screens.purpose: Opens the camera and waits for the QR code of an issuer or a verifier. Without camera permission it offers to open the device settings. In developer mode the value of a QR code can be pasted instead.

screens.name: Connection request
screens.purpose: Opened by the backend when an organization starts an exchange. It shows who is asking: name, logo, website with its domain label, public credentials ("Certifications" in the app) and ecosystems. For an organization the user already knows, it shows the interaction history instead of the warning for new connections. The user accepts or rejects the connection.

screens.name: Requester certifications
screens.purpose: Lists all public credentials of the organization that asks for a connection.

screens.name: Requester certification details
screens.purpose: Shows one public credential of the organization that asks for a connection: who issued it, its validity and its claims.

screens.name: Requester ecosystems
screens.purpose: Lists all ecosystems of the organization that asks for a connection.

screens.name: Requester ecosystem details
screens.purpose: Shows one ecosystem of the organization that asks for a connection: its description, its leader ("Ecosystem Owner" in the app) and its members.

screens.name: Credential offer
screens.purpose: Opened by the backend after the user accepts an issuer. It lists the credentials on offer. When the issuer protects the offer with a transaction code, the screen asks for it as a PIN code. The user accepts or rejects the offer.

screens.name: Share data
screens.purpose: Opened by the backend after the user accepts a verifier. It lists what the verifier asks for, with every field marked as required or optional. The user can pick another credential when several match, inspect a credential and switch optional fields off. A review of what will and will not be shared comes before anything is sent.

groups.title: Activity: connections and history
groups.description: The organizations the user has exchanged credentials with, and the history of every exchange.

screens.name: Activity tab
screens.purpose: Two lists: the connections, which are the organizations the user has exchanged credentials with, and the history of every exchange.

screens.name: Connection details
screens.purpose: Shows one organization. The summary has its website with the domain label, the first and the last time the user connected, the number of interactions, its public credentials and its ecosystems. A second tab lists the history with this organization. The menu shows the organization's DID and disconnects it, which keeps the history.

screens.name: Connection certifications
screens.purpose: Lists all public credentials of a connection.

screens.name: Connection certification details
screens.purpose: Shows one public credential of a connection: who issued it, its validity and its claims.

screens.name: Connection ecosystems
screens.purpose: Lists all ecosystems of a connection.

screens.name: Connection ecosystem details
screens.purpose: Shows one ecosystem of a connection: its description, its leader ("Ecosystem Owner" in the app) and its members.

groups.title: Settings and developer tools
groups.description: What is personal to this wallet. The profile picture at the top of the Me tab opens the settings.

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: The entry to the settings. It shows the profile picture, which the user can change or remove, and links to the profile, the app settings and "About UniMe".

screens.name: My profile
screens.purpose: Links to the profile name and offers "Delete profile", which resets the app and removes all data after a confirmation.

screens.name: Change profile name
screens.purpose: Changes the profile name.

screens.name: App settings
screens.purpose: Links to language, theme and security. Once the developer mode setting is unlocked, the screen also shows the developer mode switch and, with developer mode on, the links to DID management and key management.

screens.name: Language
screens.purpose: Changes the language of the app.

screens.name: Theme
screens.purpose: Switches between the light theme, the dark theme and following the device.

screens.name: Security
screens.purpose: Turns unlocking with biometrics on or off. The user confirms the change with the password.

screens.name: DID management
screens.purpose: Developer mode only. Shows the DID methods of the wallet and sets the preferred one.

screens.name: Key management
screens.purpose: Developer mode only. Shows the keys of the wallet and sets the preferred key type.

screens.name: About UniMe
screens.purpose: Shows the app version, the license and the terms and conditions. Tapping the logo several times unlocks the developer mode setting. In developer mode the screen also lists the versions of the specifications the wallet implements.

layouts.note: Wraps every screen. On top of the current screen it shows the progress and the result of an exchange, error messages and, in developer mode, the developer menu with the debug messages and the test profiles. It also receives deep links and follows the redirects and prompts of the backend.
Adds the bottom bar with the Me, Scan and Activity tabs.
